content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with mayonnaise is a classic dish that emerged in the mid‑20th century. The main ingredients are hard‑boiled eggs, mayonnaise, and often mustard, herbs, and spices. It is served cold as a snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first published recipe for egg salad with mayonnaise appeared in 1955 in American culinary magazines.
The salad quickly became popular in post‑war America due to its simplicity and the availability of ingredients.
Different countries add local twists: Japan uses soy sauce, Russia often adds dill and mustard.
Traditional mayonnaise is made from egg yolk, vegetable oil, vinegar, and mustard.
Egg salad is a staple in school cafeterias and picnic menus.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs provide a high‑quality complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply B12, riboflavin, and biotin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Source of choline
items.content: Choline is important for brain health and liver function.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: When made with vegetable oil, mayonnaise adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help maintain healthy vision.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg whites or yolks.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise makes the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improperly cooled salad can become a breeding ground for bacteria such as Salmonella.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg salad with mayonnaise is served as a spread on sandwiches, in salad bowls, as a filling for wraps, or as a side to meat dishes. Garnish with fresh herbs, paprika, or finely diced cucumber for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Over time the texture and smell may change, and the risk of bacterial growth increases.
